reasoning: The held APP transcription is the complete order; identity, date (May 15, 1934) and subject match the census register (inherited status 'indeterminate'), the WPA list (p.578, 'Regulations ... affecting home-workers, prescribed') and the APP mirror row. The corrected four-clause inventory is complete: the clauses are the ordering sentence, rule 1 with (a) and (b), rule 2, and the closing paragraph, and the character ranges 582-910, 912-1688, 1690-1915 and 1917-2810 cover every operative sentence, with only blank lines between them. The opening recitals and the signature block are not commands. I tested the producer's flagged characterization. The order cites Title I generally and is plausibly a section 10(a) rule; section 10(a), with its penalty, was not repealed by S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and lasted until April 1, 1936. However, the order defines its own reach by the codes. It binds only those 'subject to Codes of Fair Competition in which homework is prohibited', and only 'to the extent necessary' does it operate as a condition on code-approval orders. Rule 1 is an exception to code prohibitions of homework. Rule 2's duty attaches only to an employer engaging 'such a person', meaning a person certificated under that exception, and requires filing with a Code Authority. Once section 2 repealed the provisions that enforced codes, no one was legally subject to a code prohibition, so neither the exception nor the filing duty had a case to operate on. The surviving section 10(a) power does not by itself keep the rules operative. June 14, 1935 is therefore the best supported end for every clause, and April 1, 1936 is a later event. The duration term ('until revoked or modified by my further order or by order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery') states no date. Held texts mentioning homework (EO 6756-B, the Puerto Rico needlework code) and EO 6750-C (apprentice rules, which does not name this order) do not revoke or modify it. The claim discloses that an order of the Administrator would not appear among the held presidential texts. That limit applies equally to every order in the batch and does not make the claim wrong. Savings are confined to certificates and acts before the repeal. All quotations match.
